conventions.convention: All Moore--Penrose and Tikhonov statements are over finite matrices with scalar field restricted to \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\).
A truncated singular value is retained precisely when \(\sigma_i>\tau\); equality with the declared threshold is discarded.
Power iteration starts from a nonzero \(x_0\), while each subsequently defined iterate is normalised only after applying \(A\).

The signed Radon--Nikodym and Lebesgue-decomposition results require one increasing measurable exhaustion on which both the positive reference measure and the signed measure's total variation are finite.
A Radon--Nikodym derivative denotes an almost-everywhere equivalence class, not a distinguished pointwise representative.
A regular value permits an empty fibre; regularity is the universal condition over that fibre.

load_bearing.statement:
Under a common finite exhaustion, a signed measure decomposes as \(
u=
u_a+
u_s\), with \(
u_a\ll\mu\), \(
u_s\perp\mu\), and \(
u_a\) represented by a real density on the exhaustion pieces.
A signed measure absolutely continuous with respect to a positive measure under the common finite-exhaustion hypothesis has a measurable real density, unique up to \(\mu\)-almost-everywhere equality.
Every matrix \(A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)\), for \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\), has a unique \(A^+\) satisfying the four Penrose equations.
For \(A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)\) and \(b\in\mathbb F^m\), \(A^+b\) is a least-squares minimiser and is the unique minimiser of Euclidean norm.
If a smooth \(F:M^m\to N^n\) has constant rank \(r\) near \(p\), there are smooth local charts in which it is \((u,v)\mapsto(u,0)\).
For a smooth \(F:M^m\to N^n\), a nonempty fibre over a regular value is an embedded submanifold of codimension \(n\).

concerns.concern: For rectangular \(A\), step 1.2 writes \((UAV)B(UAV)=UA(A^+)AU^*=UAV\). The final \(U^*\) has incompatible shape: the expansion should end in \(V\), namely \(UAA^+AV=UAV\).

The statement quantifies \(A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)\) without requiring \(\mathbb F=\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), although \(A^*\), the SVD argument, and the cited pseudoinverse existence theorem use that restriction.
The statement likewise leaves \(\mathbb F\) unrestricted while using \(A^*\) and the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse; its stated field domain is therefore too broad.

The item defines a vector \(\|x\|_2\) and a matrix spectral \(\|E\|_2\), but its declared dependencies provide only an abstract induced vector norm and matrix multiplication, not the Euclidean convention or the induced operator norm.

It assumes only \(x_0\ne0\), yet states \(\mu_k=\langle Ax_k,x_k\rangle/\langle x_k,x_k\rangle=\langle Ax_k,x_k\rangle\) because every iterate is unit. The recurrence normalises \(x_{k+1}\), not \(x_0\), so the second equality fails at \(k=0\) unless \(x_0\) was also assumed unit.
The recurrence uses \(x_0\) but the definition quantifies only \(A\) and the shift \(\mu\); no nonzero initial vector is supplied.
The statement uses \(\lambda_2\) and the ratio \(|\lambda_2/\lambda_1|\) without imposing \(n\ge2\). For a \(1\times1\) matrix, \(\lambda_2\) is not defined.

The definition permits \(p=n\) but then its dominant-subspace clause invokes \(\lambda_{p+1}=\lambda_{n+1}\), which is absent from the listed eigenvalues. The spectral-gap clause needs \(p<n\) or a separate \(p=n\) case.

Step 1.1 proves \(D\rho(x)[h]=2\operatorname{Re}\langle r(x),h\rangle\). With the standard real Riemannian metric on the unit sphere, the constrained gradient is \(2r(x)\), not \(r(x)\), so the closing gradient claim and title are inaccurate.

Step 3.1 writes \(r_k=A(\alpha_kx_k)-\mu_k(\alpha_kx_k)\). The right side equals \(\alpha_k r_k\), rather than \(r_k\) unless \(\alpha_k=1\). The norm estimate can be recovered from \(|\alpha_k|=1\), but the displayed equality is false.

The title asserts local deflation, but the statement and proof establish only that a Wilkinson-shifted step remains symmetric tridiagonal. They contain neither a local hypothesis near deflation nor a bound or convergence conclusion for the trailing subdiagonal.

In step 5.1, \(\eta_s:=\eta-\eta_a\) is formed pointwise after proving only \(\eta_a(E)\le\eta(E)\). For infinite measures this can be the undefined expression \(+\infty-+\infty\), for example when both are Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R\); the proof has not defined \(\eta_s\) as a measure.

Its signed-measure case assumes only \(\nu_1,\nu_2\ll\mu\) with \(\mu\) sigma-finite, but the page's signed Radon--Nikodym derivative is defined only under the common finite-exhaustion hypothesis. Thus the displayed derivatives need not be defined for the stated domain.

It quantifies over “the absolutely continuous part of a signed measure or finite complex measure,” but the page defines that part only for signed measures under the common finite-exhaustion hypotheses. No finite-complex Lebesgue-decomposition construction is supplied, so the complex-case \(\nu_a\) and derivative are undefined.
The definition calls \(S\) an embedded \(k\)-submanifold of an \(m\)-manifold without declaring \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(0\le k\le m\); otherwise the asserted coordinate slice is not well formed.

Step 2.1 attributes openness of the projected slice-chart image to the slice condition alone. That condition identifies the slice, but openness also needs the ambient chart image to be open and the Euclidean product-topology argument.

Step 3.1 declares the Euclidean \(C^k\) coordinate diffeomorphisms supplied by the cited normal-form theorem to be smooth charts. The cited statement supplies only a chosen finite \(C^k\) regularity; an upgrade to smoothness is not given.
